mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 3% over a 3-month window signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 3.0% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median rank IC over triggered periods is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average excess return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and input costs, compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for two consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA and INDPRO YoY change < -3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered episodes compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST by more than 1% month-over-month indicates a broad-based deterioration in economic activity, which depresses corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall by >1% MoM
failure_condition: The joint trigger occurs but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in FEDFUNDS below 1% while CPIAUCSL rises above 5% for three consecutive months signals a failed easing cycle with persistent inflation, which erodes real equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL > 5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during any observed period.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average by more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA and > +0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during triggered periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% for six consecutive months signals strong retail demand, which correlates with higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA and > +2% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher during triggered periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
